body:
## Description

I suggest navigating the commit history to get a sense of the changes / review related chunks of code

* [chore: rm unused const file](https://github.com/vechain/b3tr/pull/2067/commits/04f61da547f32da65c06820d43ac6059b8b9288f)

* [refactor: infer appExists from app object](https://github.com/vechain/b3tr/pull/2067/commits/98cf73aba03675bfa927b91e897b311039bdf518)

* [refactor: update endorsement status logic to check eligibility at round start](https://github.com/vechain/b3tr/pull/2067/commits/b745cd5918e9b906aecc1fba899e3bf10bbc0b29) - see [1]

* [refactor: add blacklisted to status, update descriptions](https://github.com/vechain/b3tr/pull/2067/commits/291d788e924ece8023cabdebc50af1d9afa6487f) - see [2], [3]

* [refactor: hide endorsement top banner from app detail for blacklisted](https://github.com/vechain/b3tr/pull/2067/commits/0b87a47c692deb10271177b190acaca37f7f4743) - see [3]

* [refactor: update grace period estimation](https://github.com/vechain/b3tr/pull/2067/commits/369a8e0052a9a30fc2c5a07d1cfc018d1fcd7dcb) - see [2]

* [chore: cleanup](https://github.com/vechain/b3tr/pull/2067/commits/25afbdc6dfaae6da9b55cc3c0317b47272102de0)

* [refactor: active apps to be current alloc apps](https://github.com/vechain/b3tr/pull/2067/commits/1ef82a03f5a45592119c869c9b915e4eec27f00d) - see [4]

Closes #1984 
Closes #1985 
Closes #2048 

## Before (left) - vs - After (right)

SCREENSHOTS TAKEN SUNDAY ROUND 38

### [1] Update endorsement status logic to check eligibility at round start

By doing this, the endorsement banner will remain the same during the round, even if the app loses the endorsement in the middle of the round.

This also facilitates handling of grace period end, since endorsement status only updates after lambda `checkEndorsement` runs.

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d79c8ffe-72e2-4453-a943-43af7da0fa9c)

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/80bdcadb-6a0d-4e4f-bd1f-48a3ed3aa5c1)

### [2] Update grace period description and estimation

Previously, grace period message was calculated/displayed in relation to rounds. This PR updates the description to better explain the process and include the exact date when the grace period ends. Downside is text is longer...

```
This app lost its score and is in a 2-week grace period until Fri 04 Apr.
It will participate in allocation rounds during this time, but must be re-endorsed ahead of
the round starting after that date to continue participating.
```

**BEFORE (current)**

There are 3 versions: `roundNumber` at the start of the grace period, then `next round`, finally `current round`. Eg:

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/da20569d-b23d-4c5c-b33e-fd0f5bda701c)

**AFTER (PR proposal)**

Text remains the same.

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/549edeac-ef78-4402-80b5-8234f619cd5c)

### [3] Handling of blacklisted apps

PR updates descriptions and hides top banner. 
You can experiment with `0x091860cf708ffb26aa0b9b761b8e56178722c51223b0eb943a67df7c8d33c8f9`.

```
This app was blacklisted by the community and will not join future allocation
rounds while blacklisted.
```

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d7c50a3c-fda9-4c40-a81c-abb88cc36f0e)

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/270cfcc6-d659-4e50-bebe-f4f8f500cf1c)

### [4] What are "active" apps

We have been considering active apps all apps returned by `X2Earn.apps`. This is true if we're considering apps "Historically" active - those that ever participated in rounds. But endorsed+blacklisted apps or apps that lost endorsement will also be returned by that method.

After a short investigation, I decided to update the FE component (not the hook), to render under `Active` only apps that joined the current/ongoing round.

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/688631d0-0dc0-492c-bf52-66157287adff)

Thanks a lot if you made it here!! 🙏 🌮 🎉

author: robbepop
body:
- `wasmi_core::V128` is now available at crate root and no longer depends on `simd` crate feature.
- `wasmi_core::ValType::V128` is now available always
- `wasmi::Val` now supports `V128` variants.
- `wasmi_core::V128`'s `From` impls and `WriteAs` and `ReadAs` impls are only available with `simd` feature enabled.
- Removes forgotten `V128::to_i128` API. Use `V128::as_u128` instead.

This design allows `Val` and `ValType` to always contain the same variants and thus _not_ need `#[non_exhaustive]` annotation which can be quite disruptive to users.
This way the integration is not as disruptive, though users still have to account for the `V128` variants that now exists always. The `V128` API is very limited without the `simd` feature enabled which might be a bit disruptive for users still.

The alternative design is to include `V128` variants conditionally for `ValType` and `Val`. However, this turned out to be extremely disruptive to users and would have required to put `#[non_exhaustive]` to both `ValType` and `Val`.

author: eric1234
body:
This is similar to Ruby's "endless" method. The goal is to allow simple rules to be more compact (similar also to JavaScript's bracket-less arrow functions).

Being more compact (while still readable) allows more code to be seen at once and reduces keyword noise (lots of `end`s) and excess white space. These two things make it easier to scan and grok the grammar.

I've tested this in a project I am using Treetop for. It reduced the LOC for the Treetop files by 1/4 since a significant number of the rules were simple and could be expressed on a single line. This significantly reduced the scrolling to read the grammar.

This closes #54. See that issue for examples.

body:
I love metrolist, but sadly it is broken. I decided to port fixes from OuterTune, and ended up with this.
Additionally, I brought back the manual sync button in case automatic doesn't work for some reason, fixed a minor UI flaw on larger screens, and extended the German strings.xml.

Do note, I am pretty much unfamiliar with Kotlin and Android so it isn't perfect code.

This pull request should fix: 

#396
#394
#326 
#230 
#333 
#337 
#324 

Below are a few screenshots of the continuation fixes in action

![Bildschirmfoto vom 2025-03-23 20-48-03](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/085dc9b1-ab87-448a-9224-bcd91e891d94)
![Bildschirmfoto vom 2025-03-23 20-49-50](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ec3f7d6b-e9ea-425d-812a-20afbda8a0c5)
![Bildschirmfoto vom 2025-03-23 20-50-03](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/11164c37-0cc0-46f4-9e69-2a43b078e24e)
![Bildschirmfoto vom 2025-03-23 20-50-40](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f17a4c81-6f91-4ca7-9ede-aa9d2cd4213d)

Here's some known issues:

- privately uploaded media (in youtube music web click 3 dots and upload) will only be playable from a link or within a playlist, the artist and albums dont show up in Library tab. the artist page for these is missing some functionality and album pages are highly experimental. publicly available media is unaffected.
- User must sign in otherwise will encounter "Sign in to confirm you're not a bot" error
- Max (beta) quality option stops working after a few skips
- creating a synced playlist within metrolist is broken (it was already before this)
- user must click playlists in library atleast once to load playlists
- artists will always show up with less or no songs liked in library, despite not truthy
- Sync needs rework, looking forward to Outertune sync v3: https://github.com/OuterTune/OuterTune/pull/333

If anyone actually know what they're doing and have time, please help and improve this.
For now, these changes will make metrolist at least usable.


Want to test? You can use the debug APK I made, or pull my code and build it yourself.
Note, it is a bit laggy since it's debuggable. when built for release that is no longer an issue.

[metrolist-pocoguy-fix.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/19411139/metrolist-pocoguy-fix.zip)

I fully grant the maintainers to make changes to my pull request as needed.

body:
## About The Pull Request
Ports the Quick IC Spawning using Ctrl+LMB from Nova.
Admins now can quickly spawn themselves, or other players, into the game in a more "In-Character" way, either by dropping down in a drop pod, or by giving the impression of teleportation using sparkles, with this PR also comes the "Bluespace Tech" outfit, a more IC (although done cheaply) way for Admins to intervene in the round should they need it.
Also comes with a new spell to quickly remove your character from the game that can be given to both Admins and players.
## Why It's Good For The Game
Staff will no longer need to use "Select Equipment" on ghosts to put players in the round, should be more useful if you're often putting players into the game temporarily as you'll be given the option to give them the "Return" spell, which will delete them with all their items.
## Changelog
:cl:
add: Added the ability to quickly spawn players into the game using Ctrl+LMB.
add: Added the Bluespace Tech outfit, a more IC way for Admins to intervene in the round.
/:cl:

author: cgettys
body:
- Default (likely 6 if version of Python is new enough) for ZLIB compression appears to be too much CPU for too little benefit - 2 should be better
- Avoid a try-except where we could use an if
- Avoid some intermediate buffers living longer than they need to (probably won't help much)
- Add __slots__ to a class
- Simplify some if not None
- Don't capture a backtrace in a happy path, it's expensive
- Make the children a bit nicer to hopefully ensure the main webserver takes priority over them if there's contention (maybe should make configurable? not sure)

author: rodrigosnader
body:
- Added support for processing PDF files using the unstructured library in the FileComponent.
- Updated the process_file method to return a list of Data objects when processing PDFs.
- Introduced a new private method _process_pdf_with_unstructured to handle PDF extraction and conversion to Data objects.
- Updated pyproject.toml to include the unstructured library as a dependency for PDF processing.
- Refactored starter project JSON files to ensure compatibility with the new data structure.

author: jochie
body:
- Reorganized data/ folders so there are now dev/ and prod/ sub-folders
- Added a state_folder configuration entry, and ensure it exists
- Changed clean_urls() to return a list instead of a set, which is how we're using it anyway, and it can be sorted
- Track the list of URLs in <state-dir>/url_list.<subdomain>.list
- Track the previous results of warc retrieve attempts in <state-dir>/fetched.<subdomain>.json
- Write the (previous, or current run) failed URLs in failed_URLs.txt
- Experimentally use limit=-1 and to=20250119 filters in get_warc_url() and get_best_date_for_url(), which should return just one most recent match with the date-restriction given
- download_warc_cdx_toolkit() now return a list of warc files (if any
      were written) and a flag (boolean) to give a clue whether there were
      problems. This has a lot of room for improvement, but is a start.
- process_cdc_urls() checks against, and writes to the fetched.*.json
      files, to avoid fetching the same data repeatedly while debugging.
- Sorting the list of URLs, so we'll hopefully get the higher level
      pages earlier on in the process. No difference in the long run but
      may help while developing/debugging.

author: amilcarlucas
body:
This pull request includes several changes aimed at refactoring and improving the codebase, particularly focusing on simplifying methods and enhancing test coverage. author: svenski123
body:
## Motivation

Specifying an access list via the `--access-list` command line option did not show any change in gas cost in `cast call --trace`, whereas with `cast call` without tracing and `cast send` the expected gas cost changes were observed.

On closer inspection, it became apparent that the `--trace` option to `cast call` actually caused the command to spawn an internal forked EVM to run the transaction, and the access list wasn't configured in the tracing EVM.

## Solution

Set the access list in the executor's environment.

author: ppaglilla
body:
## Description

Proposal to add support for Trino installations using dynamic catalogs to periodically refresh catalogs from the configured `CatalogStore`. It allows Trino to periodically list the catalogs available in the `CatalogStore` and add/remove/update the available catalogs accordingly.

The objective of this proposed change is to allow administrators to externally manage dynamic catalogs and have Trino periodically sync to their configuration, rather than needing to push catalog changes to Trino through `CREATE/DROP CATALOG` statements.

Catalog refreshes are disabled by default and can be enabled through the `catalog.refresh.enabled` configuration property. The refresh interval defaults to 60 seconds and can be configured through the `catalog.refresh.refresh-interval`

Example configuration:

```
catalog.management=dynamic
catalog.refresh.enabled=true
catalog.refresh.refresh-interval=60s
catalog.store=my_catalog_store
```

I would love to hear feedback on whether this change is welcome and on the approach itself. I would also appreciate any recommendations on how to effectively test the change.

## Additional context and related issues

Catalog refreshes are implemented in the `CoordinatorDynamicCatalogManager::refreshCatalogs()` method. The approach is to list the catalogs from the catalog store, compare them to the currently active catalogs and determine the catalogs that were added, removed or updated. With that information, update the catalog state accordingly.

Catalog refreshing is triggered by the `CatalogRefreshTask`, which works very similarly to the existing `CatalogPruneTask`.

author: mrjul
body:
## What does the pull request do?
When `UseLayoutRounding == false` (which isn't the default), it's possible that anti-aliasing causes some borders to be rendered one pixel out of their bounds by Skia. Being out of bounds, the extra pixels aren't cleared when the visual moves or disappears.

This PR extends the dirty rectangle by 1px in this case.
It does _not_ change the visual bounds.

The new behavior is triggered as long as `UseLayoutRounding` is disabled and anti-aliasing is enabled. This PR does _not_ try to apply advanced heuristics to minimize the dirty rects. The exact situation when the out-of-bounds draw is triggered could be quite complex to figure out. Blitting two extra rows and columns of pixels instead should be acceptable.

## Fixed issues
 - Fixes #12157

author: thisaay
body:
## Summary

This pull request expands support for preview functions in the KSP processor.  
Previously, only functions annotated with `@ArkiveComposable` were handled — now all `@Preview`-like annotations are also supported.

## Changes

### Type

- [x] **Feature**: This pull request introduces a new feature.

### Description

- Added support for collecting all functions annotated with `@Preview`, including custom annotations like `@PreviewLightDark`.
- Since KSP does not support inherited (meta) annotations, the workaround involves:
  - Scanning all functions annotated with `@Composable`.
  - Checking if they contain a direct `@Preview` annotation to extract metadata (e.g. `name`, `group`).
  - If not, look for annotations whose names start with `"Preview"`.
- Priority is given to `@ArkiveComposable`. If it is present, other previews are ignored as `@ArkiveComposable` provides more complete metadata.
- Introduced a new `ksp` option: `skipPreviews`  
  This allows users to skip preview processing entirely, if needed.

author: jmaralo
body:
I tried to move around a couple things in hopes of improving how the encoder works. Apart from that the PR includes a small fix on a reorder warning I got on the cabinet HVSCU.

I haven't tested it yet, but I will try to do so tomorrow.

**TL;DR: Call the read method of the encoder sensor in a cyclic action!**

Here is a long rant on how the encoder currently works.

The main feature on top of the regular Encoder is that the EncoderSensor calculates the position, speed and acceleration from the Encoder counter. To do so it has to perform two derivatives.

The position is simple, subtract the current counter value from the starting one and multiply by the meters each counter step represent.

Now, for the speed and acceleration, there is a neat trick to calculate both with three position samples equally spaced apart (for example the position now, the position 10ms ago and the position 20ms ago). I don't properly understand the math, but @ricardochust told me about it and it made sense. It basically does some operations on the three positions and has less error than taking just two points and making two derivatives on it.

Each time the read method is called this process is repeated and it EXPECTS THAT THE METHOD IS CALLED IN REGULAR TIME INTERVALS (inside a cyclic action). The previous version had a protection but I decided to remove it for now.

Internally the EncoderSensor stores multiple position samples in a ring buffer and uses the last and mid-point of the ring buffer to do the calculations, this is because if the points are too close by it could lead to errors, but maybe the refresh rate has to be high, so maybe you want to take points spaced 500ms away but refresh the position, speed and acceleration each 10ms, to do so you would need to call the read method each 10ms and set the EncoderSensor samples to 100 (half point is 50 * 10ms -> 500ms in the past).

If this didn't make any sense I understand :)

author: matanlurey
body:
This is based off a discussion between me and @jtmcdole that I thought I filed a bug for, but I guess I did not. Basically, we can sometimes have "In Progress" tasks where LUCI had sent as an updated build status, and for one reason or another, we dropped it on the floor.

This re-uses the existing checks and also asks LUCI if we seem to have dropped something.

author: redth
body:
Adds a new ILoggerProvider to the McpServer's logging factory which can then relay server logs which occur within the System.Extensions.Logging pattern back to the client via a notification message as per the spec.

## Motivation and Context
I started writing this code before I saw #53 was merged and now see #59 open, so thought I'd push this code up anyway even if it's ultimately just throwaway code.

## How Has This Been Tested?
Not yet

## Breaking Changes
Logging from the server now will all go back to the client, so it is more a behavioural change, but could be unexpected noise.

- [ ] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

- [x] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to change)
- [ ] Documentation update

author: ahu96
body:
Currently, error report only contains the stacktrace of the error but sometimes it's very useful to have a log buffer containing logs right before the error (ie knowing the commit failed is not very useful but the recent logs will tell us that it's actually because pre-commit failed which is actually useful for debugging) 

Add a handler for storing and add recent logs to error report
